name: Diagnostic_EQN-SIM_2
generalfeedback: We are given \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:0}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:1}}\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:2}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:3}}\mbox{.} \end{array}\] Multiplying the first equation by {{CT:4}} and the second equation by {{CT:5}} we obtain \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:6}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:7}}\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:8}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:9}}\mbox{.} \end{array}\] Subtracting the latter equation from the former one we find \[ x=\frac{{{CT:7}} - {{CT:9}}}{{{CT:10}} - {{CT:11}}} = \frac{{CT:12}}{{CT:13}} = {{CT:14}} \] and then substituting \(x={{CT:14}}\) in the former equation we see \[y = \frac{{{CT:7}} - {{CT:10}} \times {{CT:15}}}{{CT:16}} = \frac{{CT:17}}{{CT:16}} = {{CT:18}}\mbox{.}\]

on_true.feedback: You can check your answer by substituting for \(x\) and \(y\) and confirming that the equations balance.

on_false.feedback:
Substituting \(x={@ans1@}\) and \(y={@ans2@}\)
\[{{CT:0}}={@ansg1@}\]
\[{{CT:2}}={@ansg2@}\] but substituting in the unique correct values for \(x\) and \(y\) the above equations should evaluate to {{CT:19}} and {{CT:20}} respectively.

on_true.feedback: When you multiply an equation by a constant, remember to multiply both sides, the right hand-side as well as the left hand-side.
It may be that you added the two equations when you should have subtracted one from the other.
